title: Utica Greens
subtitle: Escarole with cherry peppers, prosciutto and breadcrumbs
excerpt: Escarole braised with garlic, pickled cherry peppers and prosciutto, then finished with crisp breadcrumbs and parmesan. A regional Italian-American side dish from upstate New York.
sourceNotes: Classic dish from Utica, New York, popularised by chef Joe Morelle. Synthesised from multiple local and home cook sources.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Braise the greens up to a day ahead. Add the breadcrumbs and grill just before serving.

content.text: Utica greens are a punchy Italian-American side. Bitter escarole softens in garlicky oil with salty prosciutto and pickled peppers. The breadcrumb topping adds the crunch that keeps it interesting.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Blanch the escarole for 2 minutes. Drain well and squeeze out the excess water with your hands.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the olive oil in a wide frying pan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute until pale gold.
Add the prosciutto and cook for 2 minutes until it starts to crisp at the edges.
Add the pickled peppers and chilli flakes. Stir for 1 minute. Add the escarole and toss everything together.
Pour in the stock. Cook on a medium heat for 5 minutes until the escarole is tender and most of the liquid has gone.
Meanwhile, toast the breadcrumbs in the remaining tablespoon of oil in a small pan until golden. Remove from the heat and stir in the parmesan and pecorino.
Transfer the greens to a serving dish. Scatter the cheesy crumbs over the top and serve straight away.

items.cause: The blanched escarole was not squeezed dry enough.
items.fix: Press the blanched leaves firmly in a colander, then gather them in your hands and squeeze hard before they go into the pan.

items.cause: The escarole was not blanched long enough.
items.fix: Blanch for a full 3 minutes next time. The salt in the prosciutto and cheese also balances the bitterness.

items.cause: They were added too early and absorbed moisture from the greens.
items.fix: Toast and add the crumbs only at the last moment, right before serving.
